source.version: NBER Working Paper 33641, April 2025 (p. 1). This is not the latest version: the candidate record lists the Organization Science 2026 article (doi 10.1287/orsc.2025.20702), whose abstract reportedly gives N = 791, and a shorter title. The retrieval entry has no version_saved field.
source.title_on_document: The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI Reshaping Teamwork and Expertise

supplement.where: The text refers to an 'Appendix' for AI-generated evaluations (p. 13, fn. 11). The appendix in this PDF (pp. 47-54) holds problem statements, the evaluation process, prompts, and Figure A1, but not the AI-evaluation results.
supplement.holds: Robustness results using AI-generated evaluations (p. 13, fn. 11). Results for expert-rated novelty, feasibility, and impact are described as confirming the main findings (p. 11) but no numbers for them are printed anywhere in this PDF.

paper_design_summary: Procter & Gamble Commercial and R&D professionals in a one-day virtual product development workshop were randomly assigned in a 2x2 design to work alone or in a cross-functional two-person team, with or without a GPT-4-based AI tool, on a real business-unit innovation problem. Blind expert evaluators rated each submitted solution (550 solutions) for overall quality (primary), novelty, feasibility, impact, business potential, and technicality; the paper also reports solution length, time spent, self-reported emotions, and a figure of semantic similarity of solutions within each condition.

studies.label: P&G field experiment (2x2: individual/team x no AI/AI), product innovation solutions

assignment.what_was_assigned: Individuals were assigned to one of four conditions: individual without AI (control), team (R&D + Commercial) without AI, individual + AI, team + AI. Teams were formed by randomly pairing one Commercial and one R&D professional. After the first task, control-group participants received AI training and repeated the task with AI (crossover); primary results use only the first, between-subject task.
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to these conditions within each of the eight randomization clusters, defined by four business units (Baby Care, Feminine Care, Grooming, and Oral Care) across two geographies (Europe and Americas).
assignment.locator: p. 9, Section 3.2; p. 10 (stratification, random pairing); p. 11, Section 3.3 (crossover for control groups)
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 2 (AEA RCT registry trial 13603); p. 8, fn. 3 (AEARCTR-0013603, plan embargoed until acceptance)

arms.name: Team No AI (T1)
arms.description: Two-person team (one R&D + one Commercial) without AI

arms.name: Individual + AI (T2)
arms.description: Individual with GPT-4-based AI tool and one-hour prompting training

arms.name: Team + AI (T3)
arms.description: Two-person team (one R&D + one Commercial) with GPT-4-based AI tool and one-hour prompting training

participants.exclusions: 811 people took part; 35 were not randomly assigned (late entrants did the task alone without AI; people above band 3 did the task alone with AI) and are excluded from the main analysis (p. 9, fn. 6). Individuals from incomplete teams were reassigned to individual assignments (p. 10, fn. 8). The text gives 776 randomized; Table 1 (p. 41) lists 154 + 155 individuals and 230 (115 teams) + 252 (126 teams) team participants, which sum to 791 people and 550 solutions (matching the 550 observations in Table 2). The 791 is my sum of Table 1 counts; the paper does not reconcile it with 776.
participants.who: Experienced Commercial and R&D professionals at Procter & Gamble in four business units (Baby Care, Feminine Care, Grooming, Oral Care)
participants.country: Not stated by country; Europe and Americas
participants.quote: Our analyses focus on 776 of these participants who were randomly assigned across four conditions.
participants.locator: p. 9, Section 3.2 and fn. 6; p. 41, Table 1; abstract p. 2 (776 professionals)

ai_tool.name_model: GenAI tool built on GPT-4 accessed through Microsoft Azure; July workshop participants had GPT-4o (p. 10, fn. 10)
ai_tool.how_used: Participants used the tool as they saw fit after a one-hour training on prompting, led by an author, with a PDF of recommended prompts (ideation, framing, simulated customer interview prompts; Appendix C, pp. 50-53).

task.description: Develop a new solution (new products, packaging, communication, retail execution) to a real business-unit innovation problem statement; the solution has an idea name, recommended solution, rationale, critical work required, and resources needed (Appendix A-B, pp. 47-48).
task.duration: One-day virtual workshop; exact task time limit not stated

outcomes.name: Solution Quality (standardized)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Overall quality on a 1-10 scale by blind expert evaluators (22 evaluators, MBA and engineering students or recent graduates; 1,595 evaluations of 550 solutions, about 2.89 per solution; averaged per solution; ICC2 = 0.452), standardized on the individual-no-AI control group. Feasibility, impact, and business potential were rated in the same process; the paper says novelty, feasibility, and impact confirm the main findings but prints no numbers. AI-generated evaluations are a robustness check reported in an appendix not in this PDF. Three specifications: no controls, business-unit and date FE, FE plus controls; robust SEs.

contrasts.reported: Individual + AI coefficient 0.373*** (0.106) [Model 1], 0.386*** (0.108) [FE], 0.370*** (0.107) [FE + controls]; Control Mean 0.000 (0.081) in Model 1; Observations 550; outcome standardized on control group. Text: 0.37 SD increase (p < 0.01).

Both relative to Individual No AI: Team + AI 0.392*** (0.122) vs Team No AI 0.245** (0.120) [Model 1]; 0.404 (0.123) vs 0.262 (0.122) [FE]; 0.463 (0.139) vs 0.307 (0.131) [FE + controls]. Test Team+AI = Team No AI: p = 0.242, 0.254, 0.216.

outcomes.name: Novelty (expert-rated)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Degree of innovation and originality, 1-10 scale, rated by the same blind expert evaluators at the same time as quality. Reported only as a robustness check with no numbers printed.

contrasts.reported: No numbers printed. Text: 'we also collected information on solution novelty, feasibility, and impact as robustness checks. These measures confirm the findings reported in the main text.' Direction inferred from that sentence only.
contrasts.locator: pp. 10-11, end of Section 3.2; p. 13, Section 4.2

outcomes.name: Semantic similarity between solutions (distance from mean)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Kernel density of each solution's distance from the condition mean in sentence-embedding space (cosine distance; x-axis labelled 'Distance from Mean (Squared Units)'); lower values mean higher similarity. Also includes an 'AI Only' set of GPT-4o solutions generated by prompting with the problem instructions.

contrasts.reported: Figure only, no numbers or test. Text: 'While human-only solutions (both individual and pair) show relatively dispersed distributions, AI-aided solutions demonstrate notably higher semantic similarity.' Sign reversed: higher similarity = lower diversity.
Figure only, no numbers or test; Pair + AI density sits at lower distance from mean than Pair. Sign reversed: higher similarity = lower diversity.

contrasts.control_arm: AI-aided human solutions (Alone + AI, Pair + AI)
contrasts.reported: Figure only. Text: 'This "AI Only" shows much tighter clustering, suggesting that human participants are not simply transcribing naive AI outputs.' Number of AI Only outputs not stated.
contrasts.locator: p. 40, Figure 13; p. 19, Section 6.4 and fn. 14

diversity_detail.metric: Distance of each solution from the mean (centroid) of its condition in sentence-embedding space, cosine distance; shown as kernel densities
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each solution against its condition's mean, within each of the four conditions plus an AI Only set
diversity_detail.uncertainty: None reported; no test or interval
diversity_detail.notes: Whether all 550 solutions enter the figure is not stated. Wording mixes 'similarity' and 'distance'; the figure note says lower values indicate higher similarity.

outcomes.name: Top 10% Solutions (probability of being rated in top decile of quality)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Binary: 1 if the solution's expert quality score (1-10) ranks in the highest decile of all submissions. Linear probability model, three specifications.

contrasts.reported: Individual + AI 0.019 (0.029) [Model 1], 0.029 (0.029) [FE], 0.030 (0.029) [FE + controls]; Control Mean 0.058; Observations 550.

Relative to Individual No AI: Team + AI 0.092** (0.037) vs Team No AI 0.037 (0.033) [Model 1]; 0.098 (0.038) vs 0.045 (0.034) [FE]; 0.112 (0.045) vs 0.054 (0.041) [FE + controls]. Test Team+AI = Team No AI: p = 0.190, 0.207, 0.175.

outcomes.name: Solution Length (words)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Total number of words in the submitted solution (a computed count; no codebook measure fits exactly).

contrasts.reported: Individual + AI 504.507*** (42.963) [Model 1], 511.568*** (45.206) [FE], 503.833*** (45.081) [FE + controls]; Control Mean 381.422 [Model 1]; Observations 550.
Relative to Individual No AI: Team + AI 543.745*** (42.328) vs Team No AI 30.456 (27.419) [Model 1]; no direct test of Team+AI = Team No AI printed.

outcomes.name: Technicality of solution (technical vs commercial orientation)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 Likert score by the same expert evaluators; higher = more technically oriented. Reported as distributions by participant function (Figure 6, individuals) and by team condition (Figure 11, with bimodality coefficients). Not a creativity construct; recorded because the paper reads it as breadth of expertise in the output.

contrasts.reported: Bimodality coefficient Team No AI = 0.564 vs Team + AI = 0.482; similar overall levels of technical content; no test.
Figure only: without AI, Commercial and R&D participants' technicality distributions differ; with AI the distinction disappears. No numbers.

company_involvement.description: Four co-authors (Yi Han, Jeff Goldman, Hari Nair, Stewart Taub) are Procter & Gamble employees; the experiment ran inside P&G; P&G gave financial support to the Digital Data Design Institute at HBS through gifts in 2023-2025; Karim Lakhani was a paid consultant for P&G in 2021-2022.

eligibility.reason: Field RCT: professionals randomly assigned to work with or without a GPT-4-based tool (alone or in teams) on product-innovation ideation (p. 9). Hundreds of people analyzed (776 randomized per text; Table 1 counts sum to 791; 550 solutions). Outcomes scored on the output by blind expert raters (quality, novelty) and by sentence-embedding similarity (diversity). Caveat: the primary outcome is overall quality, which the codebook maps to usefulness; novelty has no printed numbers and the diversity result is figure-only, so a creativity-specific estimate may need the journal version or appendix.

one_line_finding: Individuals with AI produced solutions rated 0.37 control-group SD higher in expert-rated quality than individuals without AI (0.373, SE 0.106; Table 2, p. 42), and AI-aided solutions were more semantically similar to one another than human-only solutions (Figure 13, p. 40, no test).
open_questions: Participant count: text says 776 randomized (pp. 2, 3, 9) but Table 1 counts sum to 791 (154 + 155 + 230 + 252); the journal version reportedly says 791. Which count is the analyzed sample?
Should expert-rated 'overall quality' of innovation solutions be coded usefulness (codebook wording) or overall_creativity for this ideation task?
Novelty, feasibility, and impact results and the AI-evaluation robustness check are not printed in this NBER version; check the Organization Science version and its online appendix.
Diversity (Figure 13) has no numeric arm levels or uncertainty; check the journal version for a quantified similarity result.
notes: Screened the NBER WP 33641 (April 2025). The crossover (control groups repeat the task with AI after training) is a before-after within-person comparison with AI added, not removed; the paper reports no results from it, so no after_ai outcome. Self-reported outcomes (positive and negative emotions, Tables 6-7; expected top-10% placement, Figure 10) and time spent (Table 4) are omitted because they are not scored on the output or are not creativity outcomes. Core-job heterogeneity in quality is in Table 5 (p. 43). Team-level analyses treat each team's single solution as one observation.
